skill.name: baml-integration
skill.description: Guides BAML schema design, DTO generation, client synchronization, and Python or TypeScript wrapper patterns for type-safe LLM applications.
skill.summary: Use BAML to design typed prompts, sync generated clients, and wrap LLM calls safely.

content.value_statement: LLM features often drift from application types and generated clients. This skill guides BAML schemas, DTOs, client generation, and wrappers for safer integration work.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to inspect existing BAML source directories and generator configuration.
Shows patterns for BAML classes, enums, functions, retries, and fallback clients.
Guides DTO design for Python and TypeScript generated types.
Provides schema synchronization patterns for databases, APIs, and frontend types.
Shows wrapper patterns for retries, caching, rate limiting, metrics, and errors.
Includes troubleshooting guidance for generation errors and type mismatches.
limitations: It does not install BAML or provider SDKs for the user.
It cannot guarantee generated clients match every project architecture.
It may suggest CLI commands that users should review before running.
It provides patterns, not a full production observability framework.

use_cases.title: Add Typed LLM Features
use_cases.description: Define BAML inputs, outputs, and functions before adding a new LLM workflow.

use_cases.title: Synchronize Generated Clients
use_cases.description: Keep BAML schemas aligned with database models, API contracts, and frontend types.

use_cases.title: Standardize LLM Access
use_cases.description: Wrap generated BAML clients with retries, caching, rate limits, and consistent error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect BAML Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my repository for BAML files and generated clients. Summarize the current setup and any missing generation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design Typed Output
prompt_templates.prompt: Create BAML input and output types for this LLM feature. Include clear field descriptions and enum choices where useful.

prompt_templates.title: Sync Schema Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these model changes with my BAML types. Identify fields to add, rename, or deprecate before regenerating clients.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Client Wrapper
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this BAML client wrapper for retries, caching, rate limits, metrics, and error handling. Recommend targeted improvements.

output_examples.input: A team wants to add a document analysis feature with typed LLM output.
output_examples.output: The skill would propose BAML request and response types, a function shape, and client generation steps.

output_examples.input: A generated TypeScript client no longer matches an API response type.
output_examples.output: The skill would compare schemas, identify drift, and recommend regeneration plus consumer updates.

output_examples.input: A backend service calls BAML functions directly from several handlers.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest a shared wrapper with retries, cache policy, metrics, and structured error handling.

best_practices: Define explicit BAML input and output types before writing application logic.
Regenerate clients after schema changes and verify generated files before release.
Use clear descriptions, enums, and focused DTOs to reduce ambiguous LLM output.
anti_patterns: Do not parse untyped LLM text when a BAML output type can describe the response.
Do not let generated clients drift from database, API, or frontend contracts.
Do not hide retries, caching, or rate limits inside unrelated handler code.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps teams use BAML for typed LLM prompts, generated clients, DTOs, and service wrappers.

faq.question: Does it support Python and TypeScript?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples cover generated Python and TypeScript clients and shared type patterns.

faq.question: Can it generate production code automatically?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and review guidance. Users should inspect generated clients and commands before applying changes.

faq.question: Does it replace BAML documentation?
faq.answer: No. It organizes common integration patterns and should be used with official BAML documentation.

faq.question: When should I regenerate clients?
faq.answer: Regenerate clients after changing BAML types, functions, clients, or generator configuration.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
